stories.title: Connect Media Acquires RENTV News Site, Podcasts, Events
stories.excerpt: Connect Media, a privately held media company based in Los Angeles and the nation’s largest provider of commercial real estate (CRE) news, has acquired RENTV.com, a CRE news site founded in 1998. The acquisition also includes The REview video tool, the CRE Talk podcast and RENTV conferences. Connect Media founder and CEO Daniel Ceniceros will serve as CEO of the combined company. Terms of the transaction were not disclosed. “RENTV has spent decades earning the trust of the commercial real estate community, and that kind of credibility can’t be built overnight,” said Ceniceros. “Bringing RENTV’s content, events, podcast and video capabilities, along with the people behind them, into Connect Media gives our readers, advertisers, event partners and clients a deeper and more dynamic platform. This is a strong fit for our audience and for our long-term vision.” Steve Bloom Connect Media operates across multiple business lines, including B2B news, conferences, and a full-service creative, marketing and communications agency. The company primarily serves audiences in the commercial real estate, finance and capital markets sectors, and earlier this year expanded into quick service and fast casual restaurants, retail technology, and banking B2B areas. The acquisition of RENTV strengthens Connect Media’s footprint in its core CRE sector while expanding its overall media and events platform.  The addition of RENTV expands Connect Media’s commercial real estate readership by roughly 50,000 and strengthens its presence from Texas to the West Coast. Connect Media plans to incorporate RENTV conferences in markets it has not previously served, including Seattle and San Diego, and will assume management of the 2026 Arizona State of the Market Conference, scheduled for Oct. 29 in Scottsdale, AZ. Allen Wolfsheimer Steve Bloom and Allen Wolfsheimer will join the Connect Media team. Bloom joins as VP, CRE Business Development West, and Wolfsheimer
bullets: Connect Media acquired RENTV.com, podcast, video tool, and conferences for undisclosed terms.
Acquisition adds ~50,000 readers and expands Connect's CRE footprint Texas to West Coast.
Connect plans new conferences in Seattle, San Diego; assumes 2026 Arizona State of Market.
stories.summary: Connect Media, the largest U.S. CRE news provider, acquired RENTV—a 26-year-old news site, podcast, and events platform—to consolidate its position in commercial real estate media. The deal adds approximately 50,000 readers and expands geographic reach, particularly strengthening presence from Texas to the West Coast. Connect plans to launch RENTV conferences in new markets (Seattle, San Diego) and assume management of Arizona's 2026 State of the Market conference.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. This is a media/industry consolidation play that may improve information flow and networking opportunities for developers, but does not signal demand, supply, capital availability, or cost shifts in any specific market.

stories.title: Highlights from Connect Apartments 2026 (VIDEO)
stories.excerpt: Attendees at Connect Apartments 2026, held in late September at The Biltmore in Los Angeles, had an up-close vantage point to hear from industry leaders on the opportunities and challenges seen by participants in the multifamily market across the western U.S. For those who were unable to attend, we have summarized the in-person conference in the video below. Starting with a one-on-one discussion between Daniel Ceniceros, president and CEO of Connect Media, and Ethan Penner, chairman of Hill Street Realty, the video presents insights from Chris Tourtellotte, Managing Director, Laterra Development in the “Capital Markets & Investment Strategy: Where the Money Is Moving” panel; Mitchell Hunter, Chief Revenue Officer, Trimont in the “Distressed Property Outlook” panel; Sonnet Hui, Senior Vice President, Project Management, Cumming Group in the “Developing and Operating for Today’s Renter” panel; and Amit Tyagi, principal, Gantry in the “Multifamily Finance & Lending Outlook: Navigating the New Capital Stack” discussion. The post Highlights from Connect Apartments 2026 (VIDEO) appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Connect Apartments 2026 (late September, LA) featured leaders from Hill Street, Laterra, Trimont, Cumming, Gantry.
Panels covered capital markets, distressed outlook, renter preferences, and multifamily finance/lending.
Video highlights available; suggests broad industry focus on capital stack and tenant trends.
stories.summary: Connect Apartments 2026, held in late September at The Biltmore in Los Angeles, convened multifamily executives for discussions on capital markets, distressed property outlook, renter demands, and multifamily finance. Panelists included leaders from Hill Street Realty, Laterra Development, Trimont, Cumming Group, and Gantry. Key topics centered on where capital is flowing and how to navigate the new financing landscape.
stories.impact: No direct market signal; this is industry event coverage. The prominence of "distressed property" and "new capital stack" discussions suggests developers and investors are actively calibrating underwriting and capital strategies, but the article does not reveal specific market conditions, rates, or deal flow in any metro.

stories.title: The Points Guy Takes 12K SF at 875 Avenue of the Americas in NoMad
stories.excerpt: Travel media platform The Points Guy (TPG) has swiped its corporate card at 875 Avenue of the Americas, also known as One NoMad. The operator of the travel and lifestyle website leased 11,765 square feet at the 26-story office building, at the corner of Avenue of the Americas and West 31st Street in Manhattan’s NoMad neighborhood. TPG secured the space from landlords Kaufman Organization and Beacon Capital Partners at an asking rent of $85 per square foot, according to Kaufman. The lease term spans five years and six months. Traded first reported the deal. Kaufman’s Grant Greenspan, Michael Kaufman and Benjamin Saftler negotiated the deal on the landlord’s behalf, while Cushman & Wakefield’s Jonathan Fein and Brian Decillis represented TPG. “The Points Guy is exactly the kind of dynamic, forward-thinking company that One NoMad was designed to attract,” Greenspan, principal of Kaufman’s leasing company, told Commercial Observer. It was not immediately clear whether TPG plans to relocate from its offices at Sovereign Partners’ 100 Fifth Avenue, located one block west of Union Square. The travel media platform was launched in 2010 by its founder, Brian Kelly, to help spenders leverage their credit card points on travel. The company was most recently acquired by Red Ventures, a digital media and marketing company. Kaufman and Beacon recently invested $10 million in improvements at 875 Avenue of the Americas and rebranded the prewar building as One NoMad, CO reported last year. The renovations added features designed to attract media companies, including a private theater. Other tenants at the 265,000-square-foot tower include advertising network Firefly and digital workspace marketplace Instant Group. A spokesperson for C&W declined to comment, and representatives for TPG did not immediately respond to a request. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: The Points Guy (travel media) leased 11,765 SF at 875 Avenue of Americas (One NoMad), Manhattan.
Five-and-a-half-year lease at $85/SF; landlords Kaufman Organization and Beacon Capital Partners.
Signals tech/media tenant activity in Manhattan NoMad neighborhood office market.
stories.summary: The Points Guy, a travel and lifestyle media platform, leased 11,765 square feet at One NoMad (875 Avenue of the Americas) in Manhattan's NoMad neighborhood for five years and six months at $85/SF. The deal was negotiated by Kaufman Organization and Beacon Capital Partners on behalf of landlords, with Cushman & Wakefield representing the tenant. The lease suggests landlords view NoMad as a draw for dynamic, forward-thinking companies.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. Office leasing activity in Manhattan does not directly affect apartment demand or supply, though strong office tenant demand in NoMad may reinforce the neighborhood's appeal to office workers and indirectly support residential rental demand in that submarket.

stories.title: Bank of India, IQ-EQ Sign Long-Term Leases at Midtown Tower
stories.excerpt: JLL has secured 28,762 square feet of office space through two long-term transactions at 1212 Ave. of the Americas, a 24-story Midtown office tower owned by Stawski Partners. Bank of India, New York Branch, the commercial bank owned by the Government of India, leased the entire 14,630-square-foot 12th floor in a 20-year lease. IQ-EQ Fund Services, the U.S. division of the global investor services group, signed a 10-year lease for the entire 14,132-square-foot 14th floor. The transactions come as Stawski Partners introduces a 15,000-square-foot hospitality and amenity center designed by A+I and schedule for completion in 2027 “Stawski Partners has consistently invested in 1212 Avenue of the Americas with an eye toward what tenants want next,” said Paul Glickman, vice chairman, JLL. Glickman, along with SVP Diana Biasotti, executive managing director Greg Wang and EVP Harrison Potter, represented Stawski Partners. JLL New York vice chairman Matthew Astrachan, EVPs Kristen Morgan and Seth Godnick, together with managing director Jamie Boast of JLL’s Charlotte office, represented IQ-EQ. Bank of India was represented by Chris Helgesen, Dirk Hrobsky, and Alejandro Alvarez of Cushman & Wakefield and Joseph Hilton of Joseph Hilton & Associates. The post Bank of India, IQ-EQ Sign Long-Term Leases at Midtown Tower appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Bank of India leased 14,630 SF (floor 12) for 20 years; IQ-EQ leased 14,132 SF (floor 14) for 10 years.
Both long-term leases at 1212 Avenue of Americas (Midtown), owned by Stawski Partners.
Owner adding 15,000 SF hospitality/amenity center completing 2027; signals tenant retention and upgrade.
stories.summary: Bank of India, New York Branch, signed a 20-year lease for the entire 12th floor (14,630 SF) at 1212 Avenue of the Americas in Midtown, while IQ-EQ Fund Services leased the entire 14th floor (14,132 SF) on a 10-year term. Stawski Partners, the owner, is investing in a 15,000-SF hospitality and amenity center slated for completion in 2027. The long-term leases and amenity upgrade reflect sustained demand and owner confidence in Midtown's office market.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily. These office leases do not signal residential demand or supply shifts, though sustained corporate office leasing in Midtown may support worker populations in nearby residential markets (Murray Hill, Kips Bay, etc.).

stories.title: Anaheim Deal Represents Investor’s First Multifamily Buy Since 1993
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap arranged the sale of Nine-Eighteen Apartments, a 32-unit multifamily property in Anaheim. The property sold for $7.1 million, or $221,875 per unit. “Nine-Eighteen Apartments presented a compelling opportunity to acquire a well-located multifamily asset with scale and long-term upside in the Anaheim market,” said Tyler Leeson, executive managing director investments. “The property’s strong fundamentals helped drive a successful all-cash transaction that closed within 30 days at nearly 99% of the asking price.” Leeson, Matt Kipp, Nick Kazemi and Drew Holden, investment specialists with Marcus & Millichap, marketed the property on behalf of the seller. Leeson, Kipp, Kazemi, Holden and Joe Berkson procured the buyer. Built in 1975, Nine-Eighteen Apartments is located at 918 W. Romneya Dr. and consists of 32 units totaling 25,007 rentable square feet on 0.87 acres. The buyer, making its first multifamily acquisition since 1993, plans to maximize income while holding the property as a long-term investment. The post Anaheim Deal Represents Investor’s First Multifamily Buy Since 1993 appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap sold Nine-Eighteen Apartments (32 units, Anaheim) for $7.1M ($221,875/unit).
All-cash transaction closed in 30 days at 99% asking price; buyer's first multifamily purchase since 1993.
1975-built property on 0.87 acres; buyer plans long-term hold with income maximization.
stories.summary: Nine-Eighteen Apartments, a 32-unit property built in 1975 in Anaheim, sold for $7.1 million ($221,875/unit) in an all-cash transaction that closed within 30 days. The buyer, making its first multifamily acquisition since 1993, plans to maximize income and hold the property long-term. The rapid close at near-asking price reflects buyer conviction and available capital in the small-multifamily market.
stories.impact: Demonstrates continued investor appetite for workforce/class-B multifamily in Orange County submarkets, even at modest scale (32 units). The 30-day all-cash close signals confidence in Anaheim's rental fundamentals and suggests capital is flowing toward stable, income-producing assets in Southern California's secondary markets.

stories.title: Miami Design District Owner Revives Office Project With BH3
stories.excerpt: A dormant office project within the Miami Design District luxury mall is being resurrected with BH3 Management as a partner and about 40 percent more space. The project, called the Ursa, will feature 250,000 square feet of office space and 15,000 square feet of ground-floor retail space at 30 Northeast 39th Street, facing North Miami Avenue, near the southwest corner of the open-air Design District mall. Arquitectonica and the firm of famed artist Daniel Arsham designed the 20-story development. The owners of the 18-block retail center — a partnership between Craig Robins’s Dacra and the LVMH-backed private equity firm L Catterton Real Estate — and Fort Lauderdale-based BH3 plan to break ground next year, with completion slated for 2029. A representative for the project declined to comment on the Ursa’s pre-leasing. The Miami Design District owners unveiled plans for the Ursa in 2022, just as a slew of new-market companies began opening offices in Miami in the wake of the pandemic. The 15-story development called for 180,000 square feet of office space. But the partnership failed to land office tenants and construction financing. The half-acre site remained vacant. In this new iteration, the Ursa will expand to include the neighboring 11,417-square-foot parcel along North Miami Avenue, which is owned by BH3 Management, a prominent development firm that also has a debt arm. The Ursa is just one of the new developments in the pipeline at the Miami Design District, home to Chanel, Prada and Hermes boutiques. LLast week, another office development broke ground after securing a $125 million construction loan with signed leases from the private equity firm of billionaire Josh Harris and concierge medical service Atria Health Research. Another project underway includes a 25-story condo tower and a 12-story hotel, branded by luxury hotel Fouquet’s and designed by Pritzker Prize-winning architect David Chipperfield, though construction has yet to begin. bullets: Dacra and L Catterton Real Estate (with BH3 Management) revive Ursa office project in Miami Design District.
250,000 SF office + 15,000 SF retail, 20 stories, designed by Arquitectonica and Daniel Arsham.
Groundbreaking planned 2026, completion 2029; signals capital and partnership activation on stalled development.
stories.summary: A dormant office project in Miami's Design District—called the Ursa—is being revived by Dacra, L Catterton Real Estate, and BH3 Management as a joint partnership. The development will include 250,000 SF of office space and 15,000 SF of ground-floor retail across 20 stories, with architecture by Estadounidense and Daniel Arsham. Groundbreaking is planned for 2026 with completion targeted for 2029, representing a significant capital commitment to Miami's office market.
stories.impact: Signals recovery of office development capital in Miami's luxury mixed-use markets after extended dormancy. While not multifamily, the deal suggests financial institutions and sponsors are gaining confidence in South Florida's office and mixed-use fundamentals, which may improve overall real estate financing and reduce risk premiums for multifamily developments in the same metro.

stories.title: Athletic Club Joins Tenant Roster at Muss Development’s Flushing Plaza
stories.excerpt: Muss Development LLC has completed a long-term, 23,000-square-foot retail lease with Gravity Fitness Inc. at the owner/operator’s Flushing Plaza in Flushing, Queens. Gravity Fitness, a large athletic club combining high-end strength and cardio equipment with personal training and group classes, will occupy a portion of the ground floor at the two-story office and retail complex. Opening is planned for mid-year 2027. The club will also offer a pickleball court, a rock-climbing wall, and golf simulators for virtual rounds and swing practice. Ross Spitalnick, of Muss Development, represented ownership. Steve Zhu of Compass Commercial represented the tenant. “Flushing continues to be a thriving community with an eclectic mix of commercial and retail offerings,” said Muss Development president Jason Muss. “The Gravity Fitness lease further signifies that residents are eager for healthy options that get them off their screens and into physical activity.” The post Athletic Club Joins Tenant Roster at Muss Development’s Flushing Plaza appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Gravity Fitness (athletic club) leased 23,000 SF at Muss Development's Flushing Plaza, Queens.
Long-term lease; opening mid-2027; includes pickleball, rock-climbing wall, golf simulators.
Signals demand for experiential/amenity retail in outer-borough Queens submarkets.
stories.summary: Gravity Fitness, a high-end athletic club, signed a long-term, 23,000-SF lease at Flushing Plaza in Queens, operated by Muss Development. The club will offer strength, cardio, personal training, group classes, pickleball, rock-climbing, and golf simulators, opening mid-2027. Muss Development noted this reflects strong community demand for healthy lifestyle options in Flushing.
stories.impact: Indicates tenant and consumer demand for experiential/wellness amenities in Queens' Flushing submarket. For multifamily developers, this signals strong demand for experiential retail and lifestyle amenities in outer boroughs, suggesting opportunity to develop mixed-use assets or underwrite rents higher in buildings with similar on-site fitness/wellness offerings in the Queens market.

stories.title: Coworking Firm Nomadworks Inks 34K SF at Rosen’s 122 West 27th Street
stories.excerpt: Coworking operator Nomadworks has secured a new location in Manhattan’s Chelsea neighborhood. The 33,783-square-foot lease at 122 West 27th Street establishes Nomadworks’ fourth New York City location roughly two blocks west of Madison Square Park. The future coworking space will span the entire ninth, 10th and 11th floors of the Rosen family’s 12-story office building, according to Koeppel Rosen, the landlord’s leasing and management agent. “Nomadworks is excited to continue its growth, having successfully opened 295 Madison Avenue in late 2025,” Steven Cohen, Nomadworks’ CEO, told Commercial Observer. “We see Chelsea as a natural next step, as it has a very strong community of tech and artificial intelligence companies looking for high-quality communities, which we provide.” Koeppel Rosen’s Max Koeppel represented the landlord in the deal, which was first reported by CoStar. LSL Advisors negotiated on behalf of Nomadworks. The lease, signed in early September, comes with a 16-year term, and asking rent was $32 per square foot. New York-based Nomadworks got its start in 2018 at 1216 Broadway in Manhattan’s NoMad neighborhood. The company currently operates two other locations at 240 West 40th Street in Times Square and at 295 Madison Avenue near Grand Central Terminal. The latter location, which opened its doors last November, filled up in less than six months, Cohen said. Nomadworks’ three-floor spread at 122 West 27th Street will host its suite of private offices, coworking spaces and meeting rooms, according to Cohen, as well as event spaces. The company expects to take occupancy in late January. The 135,132-square-foot office building between Avenue of the Americas and Seventh Avenue is also occupied by event planner Van Wyck & Van Wyck, employment agency America Works of New York, Howell Belanger Castelli Architects and the offices of gallerist Eden Gallery. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Nomadworks (coworking) leased 33,783 SF at 122 West 27th Street (Chelsea, Manhattan).
16-year lease on floors 9-11 at $32/SF; Nomadworks' fourth NYC location (recent 295 Madison Avenue opening).
CEO notes strong tech and AI company demand in Chelsea for high-quality community spaces.
stories.summary: Coworking operator Nomadworks secured a 33,783-SF lease spanning three full floors (9–11) at 122 West 27th Street in Manhattan's Chelsea neighborhood on a 16-year term at $32/SF. This is Nomadworks' fourth NYC location, following a recent opening at 295 Madison Avenue. CEO Steven Cohen cited robust demand from tech and AI companies seeking quality community spaces in Chelsea.
stories.impact: Reflects sustained demand for flexible office and community spaces in Manhattan from tech/AI tenants, but limited direct impact on multifamily. However, the prevalence of coworking and tech company clustering in Chelsea may signal demographic inflows of younger, higher-income workers to the neighborhood, potentially supporting residential rental demand in adjacent neighborhoods (Hell's Kitchen, Midtown South).

stories.title: L.A. Office Leasing Hits Highest Level Since 2019
stories.excerpt: Los Angeles County office leasing climbed to its highest level since 2019 during the third quarter in another sign that the market is slowly stabilizing. Tenants signed about 4 million square feet of office leases in July, August and September, up 15 percent from a year ago and 0.7 percent from the second quarter, according to Savills. Renewals drove the activity, accounting six of the quarter’s 10 largest deals. Raytheon signed the third quarter’s largest deal, renewing 144,709 square feet in El Segundo, followed by PwC’s 138,000-square-foot relocation to Century City and Pepperdine University’s 117,495-square-foot renewal near Marina del Rey and Playa Vista. Ad agency Innocean USA also relocated to 101,000 square feet in El Segundo. The leasing improvement comes with a decline in available space. Overall availability fell to 26.5 percent, down 110 basis points since the second quarter and 170 basis points from a year ago. Available sublease space fell to 6.3 million square feet from 8.7 million square feet last year for the eighth straight quarter of declining sublease supply. A lone pedestrian is seen reflected in the window of the Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce. PHOTO: Justin Sullivan/Getty Images The biggest improvements were in Century City, Beverly Hills and El Segundo, while several parts of L.A. still carry availability rates above 30 percent. Miracle Mile had the highest office availability at 39.2 percent, followed by Burbank at 37.1 percent and Culver City at 37 percent. Average asking rents slipped 0.2 percent from the second quarter but increased 0.6 percent since last year, while Class A rents rose 0.8 percent annually. Century City and Beverly Hills remained the market’s most expensive submarkets, with asking rents averaging $7.61 and $6.71 per square foot per month, respectively. Savills expects landlords in premier submarkets to retain pricing power as trophy space tightens, and concessions are likely to remain near historic highs. Gregory Cornf
bullets: Los Angeles County office leasing hit 4.0M SF in Q3 2024, highest since 2019; up 15% YoY.
Availability fell to 26.5% (down 110 bps QoQ, 170 bps YoY); sublease space down to 6.3M SF.
Renewals drove activity (6 of 10 largest deals); major leases: Raytheon (144K SF), PwC (138K SF), Pepperdine (117K SF).
stories.summary: Los Angeles County office leasing reached 4.0 million square feet in Q3 2024, the highest quarterly volume since 2019 and up 15% year-over-year, according to Savills. Available space fell to 26.5%, down 110 basis points from Q2 and 170 basis points from Q3 2023. Sublease inventory declined to 6.3 million SF from 8.7 million SF a year prior—the eighth consecutive quarterly decline. Renewals accounted for six of the ten largest deals, with major transactions from Raytheon, PwC, Pepperdine, and Innocean USA.
stories.impact: Strong office leasing and tight availability in LA County signal recovering tenant demand and lower downside risk for office landlords, which may improve CMBS and refinancing conditions across broader LA real estate. For multifamily developers, sustained office activity and employment stabilization in key submarkets (Century City, El Segundo, Playa Vista) support continued worker in-migration and rental demand in adjacent residential areas.

stories.title: Baltimore Organizations Line Up Financing for Stalled Housing Projects
stories.excerpt: Maryland city and state officials are looking to the public sector to turn back the clock on widespread urban decay in Baltimore. With the city and state already providing $1.2 billion, the Greater Baltimore Committee (GBC) is looking for an additional $100 million to help finance struggling real estate projects through a “funders’ consortium,” the organization announced Tuesday. The committee, led by GBC President and CEO Mark Anthony Thomas, is hoping to activate redevelopment of an estimated 11,800 vacant or abandoned houses as well as “tens of thousands” of vacant lots through the massive financing drive. It comes out to a total of about 37,000 properties, according to GBC. “This is an important next step in building the private sector support needed to strengthen Baltimore’s neighborhoods,” Thomas said in a statement. “For institutions looking to make an impact in Baltimore, this creates an opportunity to collaborate through GBC and support the projects and neighborhoods driving our revitalization. There is significant investment and activity already underway. We want to make it easier for capital providers to see those opportunities, work together, and help move projects that can strengthen neighborhood housing markets.” GBC is working with housing nonprofit Enterprise Community Partners to hammer out the details of its private capital strategy as well as its implementation, with the funds being made available primarily through financial institutions taking part in the program before the November launch. Organizations believe the financing will help projects in which the construction or rehabilitation costs of properties exceed the properties’ values, which seems to limit developers’ avenues for more conventional financing. bullets: Greater Baltimore Committee seeking $100M additional financing for stalled housing projects via funders' consortium.
City and state already provided $1.2B; GBC targeting 11,800 vacant/abandoned houses and tens of thousands of vacant lots (~37K properties).
Initiative aims to activate private-sector support and redevelopment of Baltimore's neighborhoods.
stories.summary: The Greater Baltimore Committee announced a major push to secure an additional $100 million in financing to activate redevelopment of an estimated 37,000 properties—including 11,800 vacant or abandoned houses and tens of thousands of vacant lots—across Baltimore. This effort builds on $1.2 billion already invested by city and state. The GBC is organizing a "funders' consortium" to attract private-sector capital and collaboration for neighborhood redevelopment.
stories.impact: Signals policy and financing attention shifting toward Baltimore's massive vacant housing inventory, creating medium-term opportunity for developers with capital and patient-return profiles. However, the 37K-property scale and heavy reliance on public-sector funding suggests Baltimore's multifamily development environment remains challenged by market fundamentals (weak demand, low rents); developers should monitor whether this financing push enables rapid occupancy and rent stabilization before entering the market, as overbuilding or continued vacancies could depress returns.
